Wendall blinks at you, as if he can't believe you just suggested that. "Very well," he says. "We start on the count of three. One...two...three." The two of you both take in a deep breath and hold it for as long as possible.

As you suspected, Wendall doesn't appear to be affected. But in a foolishly competitive attempt to beat him, you continue to hold your breath you begin to suffocate.

You slowly drop to your knees, stubbornly refusing to release your breath. Your vision begins to fade, the last image you see is Wendall's green visage before you succumb to death.

You died.

You sit on the couch and begin talking to an imaginary friend of your own creation. You chat for hours about the weather, sports, (or lack thereof), your favorite irradiated flower, and so much more. 

You start to feel a real bond with this friend, and your long ignored social needs feel fulfilled.

What do you do next?
Keep talking to the imaginary friend
Call out to see if anyone is there
Take a nap on the couch

You cautiously sneak into the nearby kitchen. As quiet as you attempt to be, the floorboards still creak noisily under your feet.

Disappointingly, there isn't much of interest in the kitchen. There are a few cans of preserved food and polluted bottled water that you grab. However, sitting on one of the countertops is a radiation suit. This could definitely help you keep out those harmful rads, but it'd be bulky to wear and heavy to carry around.

What do you do?
Leave the room without taking anything

You yell out empty bluffs that you'll totally destroy whatever's there. After a moment, you see what appears to be boiling green goo start to rise up from in-between the floorboards in front of you. 

A translucent green figure rises to the full height of a human, with its unblinking eyes staring straight at you. Frankly, it looks angry.

You quickly scan the room for something to help you.
Look for something to help you
You take the radiation suit and put it on just to be safe. After all, your Geiger counter wasn't the biggest fan of this house.
You return to the living room while wearing the radiation suit. \n\nWhat do you do?
Call out to see if anyone is there
Sit in the room until someone reveals themselves
Invent an imaginary friend to talk to to stave off the overwhelming loneliness
Take a nap on the couch

Text: You shoot at the thief and miss. The bullet whizzes straight past her. However, instead of eyeing you with fear, she now looks angry. Instead of being on the defensive, you get the impression she will now be offensive.
You threaten the thief with the gun, telling her that you will shoot her if she doesn't give back your belongings. She pleads with you to listen to her.
You tell the thief that she's a slimey, rotten, grubby-handed thug for stealing your stuff. She looks a bit guilty, but asks that you please hear her out before judging her too harshly.

You throw your rock at the thief. It hits her on the arm and she holds rubs her bicep, saying "Ow!" She doesn't look particularly harmed. She glares at you and says, "Really? Was that truly necessary?"
You demand an explanation for her actions. She asks you to please calm down, and says that she'll tell you everything.
You use the fork to slash a hole in her tent as revenge. She is both shocked and annoyed by this, but yells at you to stop and asks for you to hear her out.

You indignantly approach the thief, sock extended. She's too confused to react. You slap her across the face with your tube sock. She stands there, befuddled.

"What did you just do that for?" she asks.

"I'm not really sure," you reply. "I just wanted to see what would happen."

You put the sock on your hand and name him, "Mr. Sock." You put on a charming yet very odd puppet show about the morality of theft, the philosophical meaning of property ownership and its benefits and consequences, and explain the error of taking someone else's possessions through Mr. Sock. Too stunned to react, the thief watches in silence.

The thief sighs, and asks, "If I just give you your things back, will you stop the sock thing?" You nod eagerly in reply. She steps aside and allows you to retrieve your belongings. On your way out, she mutters, "Please never come back here again."

The magic of sock puppet theater managed to win you back all of your things. Maybe it's not the most heroic solution, but it IS the most creative one.
You listen to the patient's heart. It appears to be beating just fine. You tell the patient that his heart sounds fine, but feel a bit nervous. This didn't tell you anything you needed to know.

You listen to the patient's lungs. While his breathing is steady, it's labored. His lungs don't appear to be filling to full capacity. This likely isn't due to a blockage, but his own inability to do so. The infection has probably spread internally, which makes breathing painful.

You give the patient a generous dose of antibiotics. This is really his best bet at recovery. He thanks you as he swallows his first dose. It'll really take about a week of monitoring his condition before you can really determine whether or not he's healing.\n\nHe then turns to you and asks what his diagnosis is.

You halve the right dosage and tell the patient this is all he'll need. He looks at you suspiciously, but shrugs and says "you're the doctor, after all." He takes his first dose. \n\nHe then turns to you and asks what his diagnosis is.
You give the poster to the patient. He confusedly says "Thank you?" and takes it. He asks if you actually have a diagnosis for him.

You unfurl the poster and present it to the patient. You explain how life is like a branch we all cling to, and that in our hearts, we are all just kittens clinging onto what little hope we have. It's important to never let go no matter how much our paws may slip.\n\nThe patient bluntly asks what this has to do with anything, and says he'd just like to know what's wrong with him.
You decide to amputate a random limb. You strap the patient down and go ahead and cut away at his arm, claiming through it all that you know what you're doing.

You ask the patient if any of his limbs hurt. He responds that his arm has been hurting a little. You strap him down and immediately start to amputate his arm. The patient screams in pain and demands that you stop, but you just reply that this is just the treatment working.

What did you think would happen when you decided to amputate someone's healthy limb? The procedure was utterly ineffective and unsuccessful. The patient is still in a sorry condition, and is now bleeding out. You need to act fast, if at all.

You shoot at the thief, fatally this time. The bullet hits her straight between the eyes. She falls to her knees with an expression of disbelief on her face. She's dead on the spot.

You reclaim your belongings and return to your camp triumphantly. However, you can't help but feel like you could've resolved this in a less...deadly way. Maybe the punishment wasn't equal to the crime. 
But hey, you're eating Salisbury steak tonight!

You shoot at the thief, aiming a fatal shot. The bullet goes straight past her head, not even grazing her. You pull the trigger again, only to reveal an empty chamber. The thief hears the empty click and draws her knife.

She pursues you, now fearless in her attempts. You try to flee, but she's much faster. She catches up to you and tackles you to the ground. Before you can react, she shoves the knife straight into your heart.
You took the risk, and it blew up in your face.

"We could've talked this out," she says breathlessly, as your vision slowly fades to black.

You put on the radiation suit and investigate the reactor. The problem appears to be a failure of the coolant system. A critical issue, but not something you can't repair. Turning a knob could potentially fix this.

In your impatience, you investigate the reactor without proper protection. You begin to feel ill and your anxiety compounds as you near it, amplifying potentially psychosomatic symptoms. You retreat from the reactor in fear, unable to properly investigate it.
You pop the stick of gum in your mouth and chew on it. It's a fresh, fruity flavor. A little bit sugary, but still pretty low in calories. Not bad! Oh wait, you were supposed to be doing something.
You pocket the stick of gum after debating whether you want to eat it now or later. It may seem like a petty thought, but you would literally accept anything over fixing this stupid reactor.
You quickly scoff down the sandwich. A yummy BLT. After consuming it, your head feels a lot clearer. It's definitely easier to think now. Maybe you were low on blood sugar.

It's a beautiful specimen of sandwich artistry. The tomato slice is perfectly layered onto the lettuce, equaling the diameter of the toasted bread. There's a slight buttery smell to it, as if the butter was spread on it after toasting it. You may be an engineer, but whoever made this sandwich was an artist.

You've always been on the spiritual side. You hold up the rabbit's foot keychain and make a wish that the reactor fixes itself. It's a massive gamble to trust in a lucky keychain, but you're under an immense amount of pressure.
You kick the reactor and hop back to avoid radiation poisoning in the hopes that it fixes itself. This ALWAYS works with your television. To your great disappointment, there's no immediate reaction.

He tells you that he has a horrific pain in his side and thinks that a stab wound he incurred is infected. You tell the patient that you really appreciate his business, but that the clinic is appointment-based. He nods as if in understanding, but then asks, "how am I supposed to make an appointment in the apocalypse?"\n\nYou are at a loss here. He's not buying it.

You anxiously try to steer away the patient, apologizing for the inconvenience feverishly and making relatable comments about "Mondays, am I right?" while he pushes back and insists on being seen immediately. He tells you that he has a horrific pain in his side and thinks that a stab wound he incurred is infected.

You poke an old woman with a headache and tell her that she's going to have to get going as you have someone coming in more injured than she is. She insists that her headache is very serious and could possibly be fatal. You assure her that this is just a passing symptom and nothing to be worried about.\n\nShe becomes hostile and asks to speak to your manager. You tell her "of course" and that he'll be in next week to speak with her. She leaves in a huff and the new patient sits down on her bed. You don't have a manager.

You immediately investigate the patient's side wound. It's very obviously infected and has likely spread to the rest of his body. However, a course of antibiotics would likely do the trick. 

Unfortunately, medical supplies are extremely hard to come by these days, and the clinic has an extremely limited supply of antibiotics. Treating this patient properly would clear out almost the entire supply.

What do you do?

You try your hardest to ignore the patient. He looks at you for a moment in confusion until he realizes that this is willful. He tries waving his hand in your face to see if you react. You continue to ignore him. After five minutes of tense silence, he yells out "I know you're ignoring me!"
Try to sidestep him to prevent him from sitting down
Pretend to do your job until your shift is over
Admit you aren't sure what's wrong with him
[Lie] Tell the patient his condition is terminal
Reluctantly turn your desk into a makeshift bed
[Lie] Tell the patient you're not willing to help someone who is terminally ill

There's a chance you might be able to find a trail leading back to the culprit. You search the dirt around the tent and find a steady trail of identical footprints leading away from the camp. You could follow them and see where they go, or you could attempt to identify who it is. What do you do?

You inspect the site. The tent is totally shredded and all of your rations were looted. The thief was "nice" enough to leave behind a single bottle of purified water. Typical. The stress has left you feeling pretty dehydrated. You could drink the water, or possibly try to identify the thief based on whatever weapon they used to slash the tent.

You sit down in your destroyed tent and hold your head in your hands. Everything terrible ALWAYS happens to you, without fail. It's just like your ex in high school told you: you're cursed with bad luck. \n\nYou're deep in self-pity when you hear a rustling from the bushes outside of your tent. What do you do?
You're filled with a dangerous bravado to confront the thief. You call out in the surrounding area, egging them to come out. In response, you hear a rustling in the bushes. How do you respond?
Try to identify the thief based on the slash marks they left in the tent
Shoot into the bushes so you can continue crying in peace

Truthfully, this pill will do absolutely nothing, but it would be a waste of resources and potentially harmful to the patient if you medicated someone who wasn't truly physically ill. The patient takes the pill under the guise that it is a "cure all" for psychosomatic symptoms.

You're about to tell the patient that it may take a few days of treatment before he begins to see any results when he enthusiastically jumps up and shakes your hand. The patient tells you excitedly that his pain just washed away like a wave and he's feeling better already. He says that he's sure it's only going to get better from here.

You pass by the patient a few days later. He emphatically thanks you for your help and says that his wound has healed completely and he doesn't experience any pain anymore. He tells you that he couldn't have recovered this well without you.

You smile knowingly as you wave goodbye.

You swear that it looks exactly like the shoes the patient was wearing the day before. But surely you weren't wrong! After all, his condition wouldn't have been able to progress that quickly even if you were wrong!

Yet, he doesn't return to the clinic that day. You begin to wonder if maybe it really WAS the patient's body that you saw that morning. You continue to tell yourself that coincidences happen all the time, and that he's surely better now.

As the only member of your settlement having completed two months of medical school, you are the most qualified (surviving) doctor in the region. Your fellow settlers have placed you in charge of the settlement's clinic, which is currently packed to the brim with sick and injured patients.

A new patient shambles into the clinic, covered in makeshift bandages and grasping at their side in pain. You begin to sweat nervously as the clinic is already filled to capacity and there's no space for this person.

What do you do?
Let one of your healthier patients go to make space
Try to treat him right here and now

There's a very good chance this could be true. You think it's incredibly likely that you did actually accidentally rob her.\n\nHowever, you do really need the things she took back. What do you do now?
This whole story sounds entirely fabricated to get pity. The things she stole are rightfully yours! What are you going to do about it?
Push past her and take your stuff back
Shoot the thief, fatally this time

Fix the reactor using all of your skills and experience

You decide to give the vault suit to the child. He timidly accepts it and thanks you quietly as you help him put it on. The doctor stands there fuming, but holds his tongue. He can't criticize you for deciding to save a child's life.\n\nAfter you send the child on his way, you make your way to the reactor.

You can't bear to face the child as you hand the radiation suit to the doctor. He thanks you profusely and tells you that you've made the right decision, as saving his life will surely save others. You mutter, "sure", and head to the reactor. But you can't help but feel like you doomed an innocent child.
You take the toolkit with you and continue on to the reactor. Surely these will be of use to you later.
You are, after all, the god of engineering. Mere tools are for novices. You continue on to the reactor without them. Was this a bad decision? Surely not.

You suck up your pride and tell Rick that you wish him luck on his evacuation. He ruffles your hair patronizingly and says, "I'm sure you've got this, buddy!" You hate him.\n\nNevertheless, you continue on your way to the reactor.

You feign incompetence and plead Rick to stay, telling him that you're a sham of an engineer and can't do this without him. He stands there and debates staying for a moment.

"Maybe you're right," Rick muses. "I could fix this in a heartbeat, after all."

You have a moment to flee.

She's pretty scary when she wants to be, and you are a massive coward. You murmur, "I was just looking for something," and slink back into the maintenance wing. Social anxiety has forced you into saving the day, after all.

The vault won't be remotely habitable for hundreds of years, and its denizens will be left to perish in the Wasteland.

You flip through the reactor's manual, trying to find the best fix to the problem. Within minutes, you identify the issue. Thankfully you had turned the dial the right way after all! You get to work repairing the vault, and the emergency alert system powers down. \n\nYou pump your fists in the air and celebrate. When you retell your tale of bravery to the other denizens of the vault, no one needs to know that you did it by the book.

You flip through the reactor's manual, trying to find the best fix to the problem. While your efforts are noble, you waste precious time copiously reading through it and trying to identify the best solution. Before you can even attempt a fix, the reactor has a fullblown meltdown, killing you instantly and rendering the vault an inhospitable deathtrap. \n\nIf only you had been a bit quicker...

You choose the radiation suit. You could use it to help you investigate the reactor to protect yourself from radiation poisoning and prolong the amount of time you spend investigating it.\n\nWhat do you do?
You choose the stick of gum. It looks pretty fresh. Non-stale gum is pretty rare in the vault. You could chew it now, or save it for later.\n\nWhat do you do?
You choose the rabbit's foot keychain. It may not look like the most useful item, but it's always brought you luck in the past. Maybe it will serve you well now.\n\nWhat do you do?
You choose the sandwich. You're not really sure why you made this decision, but damn does it look good. You hear your stomach rumble.
Investigate the reactor without the suit
Make a wish on the rabbit's foot
Kick the reactor hoping it fixes itself

In a burst of clarity, you reach into your pocket and pull out a small rock and a rubber band. You fashion a makeshift slingshot and launch the rock at Atomic Adam. It miraculously hits him square in his single eye with such impressive force that it goes straight through his skull.

His face is still in a state of utter shock as he falls backward, dead as a doorknob.
You don't celebrate your success for long. You scramble to disassemble the dam and let the water pour back to the village. When you return home, the townspeople hoist you up on their shoulders and parade you through the town as their hero.

The town's children are told stories of your heroism for generations to come.

You attempt to use a lone rubber band in your pocket to fashion a slingshot to attack him with. However, you fumble with the materials for far too long. Atomic Adam reaches down and lifts you up.

"You're not really enough for a full meal," he remarks. "But as a snack? You'll do."

You scream as he tosses you into his mouth.

You feel struck with a stroke of brilliance. You taunt Atomic Adam to try to catch you if he's truly that hungry. He lumbers after you as you head right for the dam and try to balance yourself on top of it.

Atomic Adam brings down his fist in an attempt to kill you, but you leap into the water at the last moment. His massive fist crushes the dam. The rushing water carries you downstream back to the village as Atomic Adam howls in the distance in anger.

While Adam remains at large, the village rejoices in the water's return. In the coming days, they prepare their weapons and fortify their defenses. Adam may have thwarted them once, but never again.

You feel struck with a stroke of brilliance. You taunt Atomic Adam to try to catch you if he's truly that hungry. He lumbers after you as you head right for the dam and try to balance yourself on top of it.
Atomic Adam brings down his fist. 

You try to jump out of the way, but aren't quick enough. His fist comes down, crushing you without breaking the dam underneath. He picks up your broken body and remarks that he was "tenderizing the meat" 

Your last sight is his massive mouth opening, and then black.

You point at the horizon behind Atomic Adam and say, "Hey, look at that!" He turns around asking, "What? Where? I don't see anything."

Without further ado, you turn around and sprint away in the opposite direction of the village you came from. It's time to start a new life, far away from here.

As you put more and more distance between you and the hill, you can hear Adam's booming voice in the distance saying, "There's truly nothing here, unless I need to get my eye checked!"

You may not have saved the village, but you sort of saved yourself. That is, if you can find water somewhere else.

Without wasting a single moment, you turn around and run. Adam comes barreling after you. Despite being a fairly fast runner, his gargantuan legs can take massive strides. Running is pointless.\n\nHe swipes at you until he hits, sending your body flying into a nearby tree. The blunt force trauma from the impact instantly kills you, leaving you fair game for Adam.

You try once again to persuade Adam with the flower, telling him that violence only furthers his loneliness and isolation stuck up here on this hill. You ask him if he truly wants the nuke to be his only friend.

He accepts the flower this time, tears flowing from his eyes, saying that no one has ever asked him how he feels, being a big lumbering monster, and always assumes he wants to eat people. He says he doesn't even like how people taste. It's just what all the cool monsters do.

He thanks you for opening his eyes, and agrees to destroy the dam and leave the village alone if the villagers agree to let him come visit.

In the coming weeks, Adam makes his way to the village. The reception is cold and reluctant at first, but soon the villagers open up to Adam. He becomes an asset to the village, often offering to help lift heavy building materials.

He drops the "Atomic" part of his name, and comes to be known as just "Adam."

You hold up the flower, telling Adam that it isn't too late to change his ways and that maybe you can still resolve this peacefully. Adam laughs and lifts his giant foot. Your eyes widen and the flower cartoonishly flops over as the massive shadow of Adam's foot looms over you.\n\nYou scream as he stomps on the ground, crushing you to a pulp. You die instantly.

Times like this that I start feeling like a lousy bartender.

Had to deal with a barfight recently. 

Some raider pendejos coming in to spend their ill-gotten caps on some booze. Let's be honest though, they were just scouting out the place to rob us.

Well, idiots got themselves a little too drunk. Started arguing with each other over who was paying the tab. At first, I just kept my head down and my nose outta it - let them sort it.

Punches got thrown. One picked up a stool and started whacking the other with it. But then the other pulled a knife. Now I ain't gonna sit back and let a drunk maniac go on a killing spree on my watch. So, I pulled out my shotgun.

Of course, the cabron comes rushing at me. He took a slug to the chest, and that was that. Freaking out, the other one starts bolting for the door. Yanks the handle so hard the thing falls off its hinges! Haven't seen the guy since, but I'll be ready when I do.

Reminds me of my days back with the old gang... Shit was extreme, even for raiders. 

Glad I got out in one piece. Mostly.

Some freak came into the bar last night.

Didn't even see him come through the door - just looked up from cleaning the counter and there he was. Grinning from ear to ear, wider than should be possible.

He didn't greet me, in fact he said nothing at all the whole time he was here. He put exactly 10 caps on the counter, one at a time. Well, that's how much a drink costs, so, I handed him a beer.

He took the bottle and sat by the fire. For hours. Didn't speak, didn't move, didn't even drink the beer the ungrateful bastard. Only sound I heard him make was a faint chuckle under his breath. Freaked me the fuck out.

Gonna keep my shotgun real close from now on...

Display:
Finally got this place all set up and to myself. 

And even got my own terminal! 

Though reading through the old logs... sounds like folk from before had it rough. Wonder if the manager was that skeleton we found in the shed? We gave him a burial all proper like, along with the rest of the poor folks raiders got to. Took a while removing their junk I hear.

Anyways, this is it! Soon I'll be a real caravanner!

I'll finally get to see all the old pitstops my Daddy used to visit. All I gotta do is work out where to go from here, and before you know it I can get some souvenirs or a picture to send back to him. 

After all, he could sure do with a pick me up since Mamma passed. 

Hoping that seeing places they used to visit together way back before the bombs will help. Here's to a new start!

Been here a while now, and I'm always so busy minding the shop or looking after the cattle. 

Kept forgetting their names so I gave them new ones, heck they even started responding to them! Did try using hats to help tell them apart too, but the glue never would hold... On the plus side they look great on the Boozin Brahmin sign! Clyde didn't say anything, but I'm sure he just loves it.

Folks have been passing through every now and then using the Sleep Stop, buying supplies here or just getting a drink at the Boozin Brahmin. Luca is a pretty nice guy, always asking me to give Moona Lisa a tune up when he visits, and of course there's Grahm. 

Still surprised there's a friendly big green feller, and one that takes such good care of their Brahmin "Chally the Moo-Moo". He's always looking to trade whenever passing through. 

I do worry sometimes though, because we've had the odd critter wander in after the Brahmin, but luckily Clyde always deals with them. 

That Aries feller who visits Clyde sometimes said he's gonna get some guys to set up some Repeller gizmo to ward them off. 

Said some fancy talk about them using all sorts of sounds that they'll hate... like a dog whistle, I guess.

Good thing too, some passers-by mentioned seeing some kinda huge creature stalking them in the woods one night...

I'm sure once the speaker contraption is all set up and this place is safer, I can maybe see about finally journeying out a bit to get some pictures or souvenirs to send back to my Daddy.

Those dadgum speakers didn't do the trick at all! Made it worse even. We got attacked by something real big... Like real, real big. Knew this crazy plan was too good to be true.

Ah shoot, this job isn't what I expected at all! But I can't just give up and let Daddy down like that...

He even just sent a letter saying he's expecting me to reply with stories of my travels... and I just don't know what to do. The longer I leave it, the more he'll worry, and I just can't abandon this place to travel out there. Not that I'd last long alone if I did.

I should go talk to Clyde later, he's a great listener.

I still can't believe we almost lost the Pitstop all thanks to Aries and his stupid doohickies malfunctioning!

To think the speaker tower actually attracted the critters instead of scaring them away!

If it weren't for those Vault Dwellers passing through, we'd have had to abandon the place and face Vinny.

I guess I should get back to cleaning up the remains of those critters. On the upside, maybe I could salvage some bits to sell? Silver linings and all!

So I finally did it, I sent the letter to my Daddy, along with those pitstop photos that nice Vault Dweller got for me. 

I'm a little worried Daddy will be disappointed I didn't travel to those places myself, but the Vault Dweller was right, sending those photos back should be about him, not me. 

After all, the reason I wanted to do this in the first place was to bring his spirits back up, on account of him feeling pretty low ever since Momma passed. I'm hoping seeing those photos will help him heal.

So I finally did it! I sent the letter to my Daddy, along with those pitstop photos that nice Vault Dweller got for me. 

I'm feeling a little guilty about lying in the letter, and I'm hoping I didn't go overboard with the part about the Yao gaui and the clown...

Anyways, I'm sure it's fine. Like the Vault Dweller said, he has no reason to think I'm lying... and besides, I'll get out there for real one day, so this little lie doesn't matter, right? 

After all, the reason I wanted to do this in the first place was to bring his spirits back up, on account of him feeling pretty low ever since Momma passed. 

I'm hoping seeing those photos will help him heal. 

So a little lie is worth that... right?

So I finally did it, I sent the letter to my Daddy, telling him the truth about getting stuck here and all. 

Hoping he won't be disappointed in me, but the Vault Dweller was right, it was the right thing to do, and keeping the photos as a memento has added a nice change of scenery to the shop.

You know I find myself staring intently at the photos every now and then, just wondering what these places were like before all the damage. 

Like the Ferris wheel, always wanted to ride on one of those... Reckon I could scrounge up enough caps to maybe bribe Aries to build me one here some day.

Or the Bed and Breakfast, did they serve food while you sat in bed? Maybe we can try that...

Oh and the Creamery, people really went all that way for frozen dairy? We've got Brahmin, we can do that! Now only question is, where to get one of them freezing guns?

After that pep talk the nice Vault Dweller gave me, they're right.

I'm no cheater, I just need to finally get out there and get those pictures myself. No more excuses.

Burned the photos they got for me earlier to strengthen my resolve, no going back now. Okay, so I just need to march right on over to Clyde and not take no for an answer this time when I ask him to escort me. Then I just need to contact Big Bend to request the time off so someone can cover our shifts.

Besides, Daddy can wait just a little longer for my reply, where I'll finally have my own pictures and travel stories to tell him. It will be worth the wait, I'm sure of it!

That Vault Dweller may have been harsh, but they're right...

What was I thinking sending them out there to get pictures I didn't even take, just so my Daddy wouldn't know how much of a coward  I am for never leaving this place.

Finally sent the letter back to him... I just feel ashamed that I left it so long. I just hope he'll understand the situation I'm in and won't be disappointed in me.

I'm not made for this... I guess I should be happy this is my lot in life and focus on raising the cattle here.

Ten years...ten years and I thought I had escaped this dreaded town. But, no, I had to be called back. But, time is running out. It's hard watching Dad get weaker and older, so here I am, back in Atlantic City helping him in the old shop. \nHe wanted to go out to the boardwalk and have dinner to catch up, but he knows I can't stand the water. Not after watching Mom drown. I can't believe he kept the damn boat. \nI know the shop has been in our family for generations, but when Dad passes, I'm not hanging around. I'm selling this place and heading back to Nevada where it's dry. I just don't know how to tell him that.

Dad fell again today. I told him to ask me to restock the upper shelves for him, but he's just so damn stubborn. The doctor said it's just a hip fracture, but being in his 70s, they suggested he uses a cane from now on. I suggested to him that maybe it's time to retire, but he plead "not until you're ready to take over the shop Robert". He still has no idea.

I went out drinking last night with a couple old buddies from high school. I can't believe they're still hanging around, but Paul says there's good money here. \nI guess I was too drunk to realize where we were going. We clambered out of the car and were walking around. I never even thought about the sand under my feet. Alex said I went into a full screaming panic when water rushed up to my feet. They had to drag me back to the car, and took me straight home. \nI don't think they're going to be inviting me out again any time soon.

It's all over. It happened. Those fucking commies attacked us. It was horrible, the ground was shaking, and Dad was panicking. Oh my God I can't believe he's gone. \nWe thought it might have been an earthquake, but when we turned on the radio to figure out what was going on, they said we were under attack. Dad was trying to secure stuff in the shop when it came rushing in. I've never felt fear like that before. I remember seeing this wave of water and debris crashing down the street right at us. It came right through the front doors, and I ran up the stairs. Dad was stuck behind the counter begging me to help him out, but I couldn't do it. I couldn't fucking help him.\nI locked myself in here and just huddled in the corner and cried. It's been about 8 hours now, and there's no way Dad survived. IT JUST HAD TO BE FUCKING WATER!

I woke up this morning, and for a few seconds, it was like none of this had happened. And then I realized I could hear people yelling from other trapped buildings. The water level is still nearly to the second floor. I don't know what I'm going to do. There's only about a weeks' worth of food here.

I don't know how much longer I can stand the smell of Dad's waterlogged body in the stairwell. I actually came close to leaving today when a rescue boat came by. They said there were safe places left near the Entertainment District, but I couldn't bear to climb into that boat. What happens if it tipped over or sank? I couldn't do it. Besides, it's probably only a few more days until the water washes away, right?

I have since been moved to "The Science Team" as Mayor Day calls us, and I'm now in charge of setting up a water monitoring and purification system. I was never much fond of her or her political decisions, but clean water after what just happened is the first good decision that has come from her. 

We've been moving as much equipment from what's left of Becknot as we can tear up, as well as any other tech from nearby buildings. It hasn't been easy rafting many of these consoles through the floodwater, and in fact, we've lost a few loads already. 

Luckily we had plenty of tradesmen survive the initial flooding, and are able to start welding together some pipework to siphon water in and out of the purification tank we're setting up in the rotunda. We should have the whole system up and running in about a month.

The water purification system is up and running sooner than originally projected. We had a few major leaks, but it all seems to be under control now. The tank has been running for a few hours, and after a day or two, we should have some actual numbers to go by.

It's been two months since the purification process has been in operation. We were initially pumping the clean water into metal and plastic drums, but as of recent, work has begun on constructing piping to run throughout town. This should cut down drastically on the issues with transportation.\n\nThe only trouble is, we are quickly running out of scavenged pipes, and scrap to make more. The settlement over in the modern side of town have been scrapping some of the more ruined buildings and hauling the metals over here. Hopefully we can construct enough piping to pump clean water over to them.

I've been hearing local banter about people getting sick and the contaminated dead sprouting fungus. Rumor has it that it's something in the filtered water, but there's also been talk of other more decayed corpses with the same symptoms. As if we didn't have enough on our plate already, now it seems we have some kind of epidemic on our hands. No one seems to have any solid clue on where this could be coming from. And unfortunately too, the few doctors we have aren't skilled botanists, so they are having a difficult time determining what it could even be.\n

Food supplies have been running low over the last year, and Mayor Day hasn't done a thing to fix it. Some of the newly formed groups over in the Entertainment District have been out raiding farms just so they can keep the tourists in their hotels happy. \n\nWell, I overheard that they picked on the wrong farmer the other week. Apparently this Tim Lane managed to fend off his farm, and then came into City Hall to confront Day about the fiasco. It's pretty common knowledge that Day has been running everything into the ground, but Mr. Lane told her to step it up, or get the Hell out. I was talking with his wife Frieda, and it sounds like the both of them could really do some good for Atlantic City.

SUBJECT: Lots of complaints...

Carly,

To say the people are getting restless would be an understatement. All aspects of their lives that they once took for granted are slowly slipping away. You NEED to do something, just, anything! Strong arm the Family, get those clowns on the Boardwalk to help out somehow, literally anything! I'm getting letter after letter of "concerned citizens" that are starting to turn into threats. Just got one from a farmer on the outskirts trying to contact you. Said the Family tried to steal his crops and kill him and his wife. If the Family's getting that desperate, you know the situation's dire.

People are starving, Carly. You can sit here in your "tower" all day playing it safe and letting the others run things while Atlantic City burns, but you and I both know what happens when people starve.

Heads roll. Government heads.

Please, for the love of God, do your job.

Jim

Trying to pick up some better productivity habits by starting a daily journal. Never been able to stick to one before, but maybe this time will be different.

Polls are showing it'll be another landslide election this year. But it always is. This city basically runs itself. Or, rather, the staff I've hired run it themselves. Now it's just a matter of riding out the next four years until I hit a nice, cushy retirement.

Then I'll have plenty of time for journaling.

=================================================
|  PROPERTY OF THE ATLANTIC CITY MAYORAL OFFICE  |
 =================================================

Missed a day. Need to get better about that.

There's been a lot of hullabaloo on the news lately about China. I can't help but feel a little uneasy. I'm sure it's just the media's fearmongering cutting through, and that all of this bravado is just political posturing. It happens all the time.

But there's just been this feeling in my gut that it's more than that. I don't know. It's probably nothing. I need to stop overthinking it. Getting my thoughts down here helped a bit, come to think of it.

=================================================
|  PROPERTY OF THE ATLANTIC CITY MAYORAL OFFICE  |
 =================================================

How fortuitous this forgotten journal would be...

So this is it. Nuclear armageddon. The end of days. The apocalypse. Things look grim, but my biggest concern isn't even the radiation. It's the fact that I, along with many in Atlantic City, are alive and kicking. They still expect me to be their mayor, to lead them and care for them. How the HELL am I supposed to do that?! I'm sorry, is there some sort of guidebook on how to lead a city during the apocalypse?

I've still got some of my staff here. And we have enough food, for now. Just need to make sure I reserve a chunk of it for myself...

=================================================
|  PROPERTY OF THE ATLANTIC CITY MAYORAL OFFICE  |
 =================================================

Today would be Valentine's Day had the world not been incinerated. Never thought I'd find myself saying that line, but here we are.

Rations are starting to thin out, and people are becoming worried. The Family assures me that they'll take care of it. We're not getting any more income from them, and I don't have the manpower to enforce any form of taxation. My staff are dropping like flies with both resignation letters and obituaries being the culprits.

I've got enough to keep me going for now. We'll just have to wait it out...

=================================================
|  PROPERTY OF THE ATLANTIC CITY MAYORAL OFFICE  |
 =================================================

There's no more food. The rations are almost all gone. For most, that is. I still have my personal supply. 

Money is worthless these days. Paper money. Some of the locals have started exchanging bottle caps, saying they picked up the habit from traders passing through. But the real trade is for food, medicine, water... things we hardly have enough of.

I'm cutting the pay of whatever staff I've got left. There just isn't enough to go around. In the meantime, I've asked the Family to send some of their people to the farms on the city outskirts and see if they can strongarm any extra crops out of them. But I'm not too hopeful they'll be able to find anything that isn't irradiated.

Decided to take a skin sample off of one of the corpses and take a look at it under a microscope. There's quite a few left over here in the Community Center from when they used to run a kids' science club before the bombs.

The cells are dead, sure, but they're animal cells, not plant cells. There's no cell wall and I can see the presence of lysosomes. But here's what gets me: there's chloroplasts! Now, I'm not exactly a biologist, but even I know that's not normal. Would explain why the Overgrown are green, though.

All this effort, and all I've figured out is why they're green. Nice.

=================================================
|           FRIEDA'S RESEARCH TERMINAL            |
 =================================================

The Overgrown have always seemed very hardy to me. A little too hardy. I decided to damage each "type" (in containment of course) and see what happens. Do they heal naturally like we do? If so, is their rate of healing faster or slower than ours? These are all important questions to have about our adversaries.

I'm not really sure what moniker to give each "type" so I just made up a few names. I call 'em Tentacles, Roadrunner, and Hulk. They don't seem wise enough to be offended anyhow.

Roadrunner: No regeneration observed alone. They seem to be totally brainless and just attack relentlessly. Doesn't even seem to register bodily harm.

Hulk: Has more intelligence than the other two. Can use weapons and doors, but still unable to communicate in any way. Shows some signs of self-preservation, but still rather stupid.

Tentacles: Basically just a floating sack of ugly. Has a follower personality and goes wherever Hulk and Roadrunner do. What IS amazing about Tentacles, is that while it rarely will heal itself, Hulk and Roadrunner show signs of tissue regeneration when in close proximity to it. It tends to prefer to follow Hulk, but will go to Roadrunner as a second option if it can't find Hulk.

It seems like the creatures have a mutual symbiotic relationship: Tentacles can't protect itself, so it relies on Hulk and Roadrunner. But Roadrunner and Hulk can't heal themselves, so that's where Tentacles comes in.

I wonder if they can communicate with each other somehow.

|           FRIEDA'S RESEARCH TERMINAL            |
 =================================================

Postulations, not meant to be accepted as truth. Some musings I have on what the Overgrown could possibly be. Or how they came to be. 
===================================================

Please select an option:

Display:
=================================================
|           FRIEDA'S RESEARCH TERMINAL            |
 =================================================

Now, technically any theory about the Overgrown could be considered "Mutation Theory" given that we only started seeing them after the bombs, but this is a more simplified, over-arching idea. Mutation Theory, in my mind, is that the Overgrown are simply a mutated species of plant (or several different species, considering they vary pretty significantly in appearance) that coincidentally became mostly bipedal (apart from the floating ones). They just HAPPENED to resemble humans, but that doesn't necessarily mean they have any ties or biological similarities to humans beyond their appearances.

While this is the most "sane" theory, it doesn't explain why some of them can do "human-like" things, like use weapons or open doors. Surely that would require some sort of superior intelligence! It also doesn't explain why their cells are animal cells, and not plant cells. They seem like some sort of corrupted hybrid of the two, which is NOT normal in the slightest.

But radiation does crazy things, doesn't it?

=================================================
|           FRIEDA'S RESEARCH TERMINAL            |
 =================================================

This is probably the craziest theory of all the ones I've had about the Overgrown. Zombie Theory is basically the idea that the Overgrown are the reanimated corpses of dead humans. As for how they become plant-like, I have no idea. But it's impossible to deny the uncanny resemblance they have to humans in both intelligence and appearance. I can't quite explain the floating ones as they clearly don't look much like us and are about as smart as a rock, but the fast ones and the big ones? Definite resemblance.

It doesn't help that when we hear about people going missing near areas where we KNOW there are Overgrown, there's suddenly an influx of even MORE Overgrown. And those people are never seen again. Could a person possibly turn into an Overgrown? How does this even work? Do they have to be dead for it to happen? Or could it even happen while alive?

This is a bit doubtful. If "Zombie Theory" is true, only dead humans should be able to turn into Overgrown. For as many people that we've lost to the Overgrown, there's been quite a few hardy individuals who have faced off against them in close quarters and won. These people should've surely "turned" after surviving the battle, but are right as rain to this day.

=================================================
|           FRIEDA'S RESEARCH TERMINAL            |
 =================================================

I must say, I give the most credence to this theory as it lines up with my studies. My "Parasite Theory" is that there is some sort of bacteria that enters a living organism, like a human, and takes over the body, corrupting it into an Overgrown. Actually, I retract the word "living" from that earlier statement. We've never seen a single instance of a living person turn into an Overgrown or show any signs of illness after exposure to them (assuming they weren't killed), so this parasitic infection would only be able to latch onto the recently deceased.

This would explain why the cells of the Overgrown's bodies are a strange hybrid between plant and animal, but never entirely one or the other. The lack of a cell wall and their overall structure tells me these were probably originally animals that were infected by a plant bacterium.

Additionally, this would ALSO tell us why Overgrown tend to vary pretty wildly in appearance and intelligence. Perhaps humans are only one of the possible "victims" of this parasite, but other organisms could fall victim to it as well.

At the end of the day, while this may sound a bit crazy, these are all just theories. All I can do is observe and rationalize, but it doesn't change the fact that we have NO idea what these things are.

All these years and Quentino remains the only person who understood what it means to choose success. To gain everything, you give up everything. You dedicate yourself. You do whatever it takes and you can't afford to look back. No one understands this but us; not even the real talented ones.

If the rest of the soldiers and capos are made men, we're the makers. We built this life, and we gifted it to them, with all its benefits and protections. Quentino handles the people, I handle the cash. Without my know-how he couldn't have done it. And so it goes that we created an empire.

It's a god damn shame I couldn't maintain our legacy, Quentino. Things turned south and I had to preserve my own life, you understand that. I can always take my leadership and rebuild something great, while their headless empire inevitably falls apart. And you? You're sitting pretty in heaven with all the luxuries we earned during life. No one can take that from you anymore.

If there's anyone in the world with bigger ambitions than Quentino, it's his sister. But Concerta's problem is that no ambition would ever be enough. Our hunger is practical, one challenge after another to be conquered, boosting us to a rightfully deserved top. Hers is some gnawing emptiness that seems it can't ever be fulfilled.

She's always whispering in Quentino's ear, treating him like a puppet to be controlled. In her mind I bet everything we built is hers. That's how I ended up like this, an empire stolen from under my nose. I underestimated her, I'll give her that. Most of all I underestimated how ruthless she had it in her to be.

What's an empire if you can't put your name on it? If you can't stick your chest out and show your family what you've created? If you can't give them the benefits? Now she's got control without any of the pride and responsibility, and that's a god damn recipe for a disaster. I bet she hasn't even thought about what she wants out of this. Just an animal craving its next kill.

Money is a means to an end, a representation of power and accomplishment. It's a method for creating a well-deserved life of luxury. But one Fabio Mondadori loves the smell of bennies for its own sake. He'd print cash just to fill an ever-expanding vault and sit on top of it.

I'm not complaining. Having a one-track motivation makes him easy to predict and control. And he's got a smooth mouth on him. Great asset for keeping the Showmen and the Munis under control.

I'll never forget when I first laid ears on my starlet. Her voice in the lounge that night was the only thing to make me feel something, really feel something, since I was a boy with hopes and dreams. That night I felt some ache of longing that stopped me in my tracks and pulled my glossy eyes to the stage. And I promised myself that whoever she was, I would give her the world like no one else could.

Nothing would stop me from fulfilling that promise. Nothing ever will. Not the bombs, not the dangers of the job, not even my own long-abandoned morals, may they rest in peace as a young fool's optimism. Only thing that could take me away from her was the work required to make our life happen. 

It was one thing after another. Now the worst has happened. But this is temporary. I'll build us up again. If I can't do it then god damn nobody could.

Ah, Vin. My firstborn, my heir, my absent protégé. Dutiful and diligent. Cares about everything. That leaves him room for absolutely nothing.

I've never seen so much god damn wasted talent. If he didn't have a heart, he could take over the city! I left all the groundwork for him. Instead he's off gallivanting with those Munis who sacrifice everything they have to give freebies to strangers. Impoverished, overworked, unrewarded. How can that be the life he wants? The life he's willing to give back to us, and to his kids in the future?

Maybe it's still too early in life for him to understand his responsibilities. I gave him everything, put all he could ever ask for right in his lap, so he doesn't understand yet what he'll be missing. And one of these days he'll meet a nice girl and want to give her the world. Then maybe it won't be too late to step him back in my shoes.

Little Abbie's had a lifelong career as a trouble magnet. One bruise, mishap, or Muni report after another. Didn't take a genius to figure she wanted my attention. So I made a bad judgment call and gave her what she wanted. A moment of weakness is what it really was. Some part of my mind went soft, forgot reality, and thought that if Vin wouldn't take to it, maybe she would.

It was never going to work out, that's the truth of it. Even if it weren't for tradition, the Family would eat her alive. She's overly brave, reckless, impressionable. Worst of all, earnest. You need an iron will to do business in the Family. Like Vin when he's standing up for some god damn societal justice case. Vin's got the right traits and the wrong morals. Abbie's got loyalty instead of morals. My daughter has more to give to this world than following capos and losing her life when she crosses the wrong one.

Only option now is to cut her out. No more jobs, no more access. Clean break. She may hate me for awhile. Maybe for a long time. But one day she'll thank me. It's my job as her father to send her on the right path.

Abbie was never supposed to touch that stuff. Never. She stuck her nose too close, I clipped it. That should have been the end of it. Any other bungling associate would have given up, turned tail, stuck their nose elsewhere. Anywhere else!

Yeah, I made a bargain! It was mine alone. I would do the dirty work, so Evelyn and Vin and Abbie could live like royalty. Wealth, power, security - it was my gift to them!

That was the deal. But the god damn Devil hid the fine print. Now he's given his real price. And there's no god damn escape. Not anymore.

However, initial trials show that it also has the same effects as most depressants. This potent combination both excites the brain and creates feelings of euphoria and mental stimulation, while completely relaxing the body. 

But make no mistake, it is HIGHLY addictive. Its effects on the human body are not to be taken lightly.

Human trials seem to be successful. I have long debated trying a bit myself to observe the effects firsthand. Of course, its highly addictive nature is a risk, but I'm sure that the effects will be lessened on someone who is well-aware of its consequences, such as myself.

The Blood lights up the brain like fireworks on the 4th of July! I've been doing some...trials...and the effects are nothing less than amazing. The Blood directly stimulates the ventromedial prefrontal cortex of the brain, which acts as a sort of "pleasure center." It's like having all of your favorite things, everything that has ever excited you in the whole world, coalesce into one substance. 

Not only that, but continuously stimulating the VPC with the same "trigger" substance creates a heavy need/reliance to seek out that substance again. With Blood, it's so potent that one single dose overwhelms the VPC.

There's so much more to be learned. I need more. I need to make more.

i wanted to write this entry to talk about the symptoms that result from using Blood. it's like your brain is constantly on fire, and you think that more Blood is like water, and when you put the Water on the Fire, it extinguishes the burn.

but more Blood makes it burn more, but the burning feels good at the same time, so you think, oh hey, i don't need to put the fire out. maybe i just want it to burn and raze my mind.

sometimes it feels like i'm being sucked into a vortex. there's no end, just the swirl, and i'm about to reach the singularity in the center of it, but there's never enough Blood to reach the singularity, and instead I am lost past the event horizon.

oh and it also causes fatigue and migraines.

you cant stop Blood. itd be like draining your body of all your actual blood and expecting to survive. but why would you even want to, the Blood feels better than my actual blood. 

why would anyone even want to stop? how did i even live before Blood? 

i cant remember but i also dont care.

Display: Can't believe I'm the one that pulled the short straw with having to maintain these damn harvester things. I think I'd rather be on janitor duty down in the Vault than doing this. At least it would be safer than being up here. I keep hearing strange noises coming from outside and it's starting to give me the willies...

It's been a few years since I've had a terminal. Hell, it's been a few years since I had to write my own entries. My old E601 Series took care of that for me. Oh how I miss the luxuries, and moreso the assistants.

Before the war, I was Keith Cooper, the wealthy CEO of Granite Wolf Insurance. Every desire I had in life, I made it happen. I realized just how... cooperative people could be if given the right... motivation. And that's exactly where I found myself last year. 

After the last survivors I was with served me no more benefit, I found a group of nomads run by a friendly leader named Chris. He was a decent guy, and led a decent group. Trouble for him was, the good times were over. People like him wouldn't last-and I made sure of it. He and I were out on a little hunting excursion when there was a little... accident. Let's just say he didn't make it back to camp with me. Lucky for everyone else, I was there to step into old Chris's place as leader. I could be a better leader in fact. I could help these idiots. 
And they could repay me the favor-I mean, what else are people for?

So there I was, having a wonderful time with two beautiful ladies when Terry came in and started causing a scene. He was unhappy with his and James' wives who were in my room relaxing, a few cocktails in hand and me around their arms. It's not my fault he was born a loser, when I was instead born a winner! He couldn't take the fact they wanted to be with me!\n\nAnyways, he starts shouting, getting angry, and causing a scene when the rest of the peasants came in to see what was going on. So I bluffed them! I said "Terry here has been trying to tear our little family apart! He wants to see everything we've all worked for crumble. He wants to hurt ME, the one who wants to help all of YOU". I couldn't believe my fuckin' eyes. Within moments, they all had Terry by different limbs and were pulling him apart! When his arms popped off! Man! I haven't laughed that hard in years! Justice really is sweet.

After last week's little Terry incident, I confirmed to myself that these idiots will already do damn near anything I say. It used to take weeks or months to gain people's trust before they started doing whatever I said. It's easier than the damn Salem Witch Trials these days! Someone causes me trouble? Boom, shot to bits. Another eats a tasty meal that should have gone to me? Smoked alive in the pit! 

The peasants have been begging to do anything I say. So I put them to work! The men do the labor, and the ladies help me out with my requests. Someone doesn't like it? They're clearly trying to destroy our family. 

However, Biff was upset with me the other night. A real shame, because he's the most useful to me. Big strong guy who manages to intimidate people before we have to kill them instead. Well he wasn't too happy with how I've been "taking advantage" of people. Luckily all I had to do was remind him how easily I could make everyone turn and kill his family, and he fell back in line. I can destroy his entire world whenever I want to. I will make anyone's life Hell if they get in my way.

I was starting to get bored with who was left out of the original group, so I gave a little speech I had been preparing. Essentially, I told everyone that who all was left was clearly the best of the best, but we needed to find more members to join our thriving family. They should go out and find new members and bring them to me. If they didn't want to be a part of the winning team, then they clearly wanted to destroy us. Into the pit they went! Made convincing a lot easier. This all worked surprisingly well, however the real fruit was the resources we were getting.

My scouts ran into an interesting group yesterday. They call themselves the Crater Raiders. Apparently they are doing pretty well for themselves, and that means a nice piece of the pie for myself if I can get in. I'll be meeting with a few of their leaders in three days to discuss deals. I dabbled a bit in the drug business before the world went to shit, so I have a few things I can bring to the table. Shouldn't be long until I'm the one calling the shots. \n\nThis Meg bitch is going to be the biggest obstacle for me though. From what I hear, she doesn't seem like the type to take orders from others. I'm sure I can find ways to make her budge. After all, I'm ALWAYS right.

Things are not running as smoothly as I had originally hoped. Many people have made the right decision to respect me due to my charming personality and good looks, but others seem to be suspicious of my intentions. My group of idiots have shuffled into the Crater Raiders well, but I however haven't been given the leadership role I deserve. 

I should be able to convince people that the other leaders are not worthy. It might take some time, but these idiots should soon see that Meg is too useless and weak to be in charge. It should be me! 

They're either with me, or against me.

Bitch all ya want, we're taking Bim and Bam for guard duty over at the chem lab - permanently.

The cook's been getting jumpy about the plants in the area and we can't let that affect her work, capiche? The job she does for us trumps anything you thimble brains think is important. Without her, there's no Blood. Without Blood, we're donezo.

You remember which building the lab's in, right? Second floor, all sealed up like, other side of city hall near that mess of pipes the Munis used to use?

Have those two report tomorrow at 0800 sharp! That's eight o'clock in the morning, in case you're too dumb to remember. And I know you are.

Found the strangest thing the other day: a slip of Old World money they call a "two-dollar bill." I'd never heard of one before... It's the damnedest thing! Looks just like a one-dollar bill, or a five or a ten, but the thing is worth TWO dollars! Least, that's what it says!

There's some kind of story here, I just know it! I can't let this discovery go un-investigated. I'm putting out a call to the whole Family - find me more two-dollar bills! Or more information on them, at least.

Anyone who does will be rewarded - generously. I'm talking a bucket full of caps. This thing must be priceless, so I'll pay a fat stack of change in return.

Can't believe the Munis have been blind enough to let us sit here right under their noses for so long. Bam said we've had this place since old TR's day. Imagine that!\n\nI'd like to see the look on Buttercup's face the day he finally finds out. Except I wouldn't, because he'd beat me to death with the shirt I'm wearing. So instead, I just imagine, and hope that day is a long, long ways off.

Seriously, can nobody tell me how the back door works? It's like magic! You just knock enough times and it opens up all on its own!? I just don't get it.\n\nThe note says not to ask, but I can't help myself. Please, somebody tell me! Ain't that some kind of security concern, after all?

Beer, 20 cases

Wine, 30 cases

10mm sub-machine guns, 2 cases

10mm ammo, 15 cases

Fine Italian tailored suits, salvaged, 5 cases

The look on Bim's face when I showed him that two-dollar bill? Priceless.

Employee Name: Harold Osborne

Mr. Osborne is a recent employee, having joined the company 5 months ago. He was hired as a general laborer, helping construct and maintain the gas extraction platform. A quiet individual, normally keeping to himself however, has lately started to completely ignore his co-workers unless he is being given a task to complete.

When confronted with these accusations Mr. Osborne is stated on record saying that they are untrue and that he is a true patriot. It is unclear why he immediately alluded to patriotism, but has been flagged by management as evidence that Mr. Osborne may be a Communist Sympathizer. 

Management has requested that we keep a close eye on him and to contact the proper authorities if we find any definitive proof of Mr. Osborne's sympathies.

Assault on Stoney Man Tower
----------------------------

When it comes the matter of expansion, as raised in the last council meeting, I have concluded that Stony Man Lookout is the most logical starting point.

The mutants have proven resistant to our messaging and regularly attack the camp. Taking over the Lookout would deal with the mutant problem once and for all. We would also gain a valuable strategic asset: a clear view of the immediate area from which to plan our next moves.

I need to plan the mission, only then can I petition to the council. Getting them to give it the go ahead should not be a problem. As a senior officer for the old regime, I carry significant sway with the them, and we have many able-bodied soldiers willing to die for the cause. This is a chance to show our strength and begin our glorious mission.

Searching the Brown House
--------------------------

Rapidan Camp is another key target for future expansion. A retreat for the former capitalist pig in chief, President Hoover, it has everything we need. Aside from the dusty old books and antiques, it has multiple secure buildings. I also remember seeing military personnel when we visited the camp in the summer before the war. Before I was shown the truth.

I will petition the council at the first opportunity.

Summary:

A fully dressed mannequin, decked out in ski gear, was discovered lying in bed beneath a blanket.

A note accompanied the scene stating, "Wrap up warm, looks like ice tonight.".

A photograph was found featuring the mannequin in the shower, taken from an unusual angle through the door frame.

In response to all this, the cleaning team was instructed to conduct a deep clean of the room, disposing of the remaining items around the back. The nature of the discoveries left all of us curious as to what might of happened here, but a collective decision was made not to delve into the mysteries surrounding the guest's choices due to fear of what we might find.

Title:
Strip Poker Incident

Summary:
ALL STAFF are required to alert casino security about guests who are starting to become disruptive. We want to avoid a repeat of the strip poker incident. 

Both hotel and casino staff allowed Mr Morrison's hijinks to continue for too long before intervening. Also, be vigilant for signs of people using the games we provide as a way of indulging in indecent behavior. The shout of "All in must mean all off!" is burned into my mind and I think we'd all benefit if we don't have to see that ever again.

I've finally managed to get this old terminal working. I "stole" it from the old park ranger office upstairs but this thing was practically junk, so sadly whatever was on it before has been lost to time.

We arrived here a few days ago and it seems there's been a few previous residents over the years, someone even took the time to taxidermy a whole new collection of animals in the displays! There's 10 of us here and as far as we know, this place is ours for now.

It'll be nice to sleep with a roof over my head, even better knowing that we're secure at least down in this basement. It even comes with beds!

We've been situated in this old visitor center for a few months now and we've managed to keep our heads low from any unwanted parties. Seems we weren't the only ones that have set up shop in Shenandoah. And I don't mean the "ghost of a park ranger" that people claim sneaks around in the tunnels here at night.\n\nA few of us went to explore the western side of the park, but the wildlife around here is too dangerous for long treks. Archie and his kid came hobbling into my office today with William's toe in a rag. Dumb kid had been playing around with his gun again, thinks himself some kind of post-apocalyptic cowboy.

We thought DC was hit bad, but at least it was quick. Whatever happened here after the war, it can't have been good and I fear for the worst if it begins to spread outwards.

We're evacuating the building.

Some kind of explosion or earthquake, unsure if nuclear, has caused the nearby hillside to collapse and now there's some kind of red storm in the sky.

Thankfully the building wasn't caught in the collapse, but we've decided it's no longer safe.

We're going to try heading north.

If the Vault is ever under high alert, the automated system from the Engineering Sector will deploy a Storm Goliath variant (Nona/Decima/Morta) to stand ready to dispose of any intruders.

With the resources at our disposal at Vault 63, the Engineering Sector will automatically construct a new unit if one should fall, allowing automatic deployment of reinforcements.

--------
Each Storm Goliath is equipped with an energy cannon which shoots electrical beams at its target. 

The secondary purpose is to fire mines at the target. Each Storm Goliath has been designated a code name to identify what variant of mines they carry.

- Storm Goliath Nona:   Fragmentation Mines
- Storm Goliath Decima: Cryogenic Mines
- Storm Goliath Morta:  Plasma Mines

------------------------------------

Self-Destruct Sequence
----------------------

This is an effective counter measure to overwhelming forces in the proximity, but also doubles as a way to keep enemies from getting their hands on our technology.

The loss of a Storm Goliath is a small price to pay considering the automated construction and deployment of new units from the Engineering Sector.


Psychological Warfare
---------------------
Each Storm Goliath has a wide vocabulary of quotes from philosophers and historical figures, which are repeated continuously during combat.

Though the selection may appear odd, the aim is to confuse and disorientate targets on the battlefield, allowing the Storm Goliath to seize those opportunities to dispose of its enemies.

Ammo Deployment
---------------
Inside compartments on the limbs of every Storm Goliath, we have installed ammo deployment containers to aid our forces during conflicts.

This feature is designed for support during warfare by helping our troops travel light and have a source to replenish their supplies on the battlefield.

Dear Diary,

So I'm giving this a try, I guess. I was told writing things down might help me "process" everything, whatever that means. Here goes. 

Today I shot and killed a woman who tried to steal some of the armor. I felt nothing. Actually, no, that's a lie. I was irritated because I had to dispose of the body, because the Deathclaws had already been fed. 

I don't know how writing that down is supposed to help, honestly, other than highlighting the fact I killed someone today, and all I felt was irritation at the inconvenience.

This sucks. Writing this down isn't helping; it's just made me realize that the only thing I have to talk to is this terminal. It's also shown me that I've become exactly like the animals that put me in this position in the first place.

I think I'll just bottle it all up in the future and grab a bounty if it gets too much. I'll either feel better, or someone will take me out. Win-win.

We got a visitor after the delivery yesterday. Said his name was Michael, and he was here "regarding" the 50 barrels that we don't know what to do with. Told us just to bury them deep, along with the food sanitizers, and not to put them close to anything important. 
We were instructed not to record their delivery and to delete any existing records.

We're also not to discuss him or anything he said with anyone... including the boss!

I don't know what this means, but I'm not getting in trouble for it. I'll keep the manifest under Admin access, just in case.

Michael came back again, same lecture as last time. 
I still don't know what we're supposed to do with these barrels 

The last batch started leaking and quickly killed off all of the surrounding plants, we had to dig them back up and move them again.

Whatever it is, it's leaving stains on the rocks, the tools... even the dirt. I guess we just keep burying them and hope it doesn't spill out again.

This is Captain R. Murphy of the Athens National Guard 

We were out on a training exercise when I received orders to return to Athens and put the town into lockdown and wait for further orders. What we initially believed were Earthquakes were in fact a nuclear attack from China. I didn't learn about the severity of the attack until we were back in town. Life as we knew it will likely never be again. 

Civilians are obviously in a complete panic, and we've done our best to restore order. We gathered everyone and brainstormed the initial steps, which seemed to help calm everyone a little knowing they had some control in this situation. We have plenty of resources, and a plethora of useful professors to aide in making Athens self-sustainable until larger order can be reestablished.

Day three and a new issue has developed. According to the Universities' Geology department, Athens is built on an ancient fault line that was believed to be dormant. The bombardment has caused stress on the plate boundaries, and consequently the old scars. Massive cracks have split in multiple areas of town, and there is growing concern of the safety of many buildings. The fractures have been observed to be shifting a few inches, making supporting structures a top priority. \n\nWe ventured into the steam tunnels below town and found that the pipes will likely not hold for very long. Professor Metter has suggested his engineering team build a water purification system in the Hocking River to supply everyone when the pipes are no longer a viable option. I've delt with some real hardasses in my time in the service, but none like that nut

The last week has not gone as smoothly as we had hoped. It's hard to tell what's fracturing faster-the town or the townsfolk. Tensions were already high between the townies and students before the bombs because of the Halloween party. This year was supposed to fortify goodwill between them, but disagreements have become yet another issue we have to deal with in this already frustrating nightmare. 

City Council has requested we utilize the protectrons to keep order and stop people from venturing out, but admittedly the students have been vastly useful in their journeys in collecting resources, intel, and bringing people to safety. The towns of Logan and Jackson have all but completely been rendered uninhabitable, and places like Nelson and Albany are refusing contact. The Abraxo Factory has been a major source of the refugees coming in, and they've discussed concerns of land poisoning due to the state of the factory. 

Although we can currently sustain the influx of survivors, older townsfolk have expressed great concern over the longevity of our resources. This is the primary cause of angst, and it's clear that as things move forward, it's only going to get worse. We've set further protocols to lock down the Armory to keep weapons off the streets and avoid catastrophe.

In a shocking turn of events this morning, everyone has been reminded of the fragility of our situation. Clearly no one has been taking this well, but the panic everyone felt when the sound of a train was heard snapped everyone out of their squabbling. 

The fractures have moved drastically in the last few weeks, shattering the rail line, and the out of control locomotive shot over the cliff causing a moment of incredible silence. The brief seconds of awe were soon ended with the commotion and destruction as the train crumpled through the old post office. Thankfully nobody was in the path, and the train was empty. 

I can't help but sit here and think of the hardships I was going through just a few months ago, and how I long for even the mundanity of divorce court. The crushing reality of Jannet's lies are nothing compared to what we're currently going through.

I'm beginning to think I might be in Hell. Where to even begin.

Supplies have been running low. The older townsfolk have been blaming the shortage of resources on refugees coming in, but have been of no help in going out to collect new supplies. Many of my men have jumped to join the efforts of collecting, because the alternative is working at the burn pit we had to dig on the East side of town. 

Despite the best efforts of the students working the water purifier, a group of men became riled up last night in one of the bars and decided to take control of the operation themselves. Unfortunately about a dozen people were killed, and the purifier was damaged beyond use. The students who understood the system were killed, and Professor Metter is nowhere to be found.

Quality of life has continued to plummet in the last few weeks since we no longer have a supply of clean water. Scavenging groups are having a much smaller member return rate as well, meaning less food and medicine. I'm told that people are slowly siphoning out to build their own groups out in the wastes. Overall, disease has been the biggest killer here, as there's something everyone has dubbed as "The Rot" which appears to be a cruel form of radiation sickness. The townies are once again blaming it on the refugees, but I have it on good authority that it's due to the polluted water. 

People are dropping dead faster than we can burn them, and it's caused new pits to be built in convenience rather than humility. I predict Athens won't be around for very much longer, and neither will I, so I'm heading out. I have no more energy to help this town, but I can at least take the key to the weapons stash to keep it out of dangerous hands. If you're reading this that means you've made it past what's left of the Armory's security, and are likely qualified to have the key. I'm heading East along the tracks to die in peace away from this mess. 

Best of luck,
Captain Robert Murphy
